changelog: Insert a narrow, targeted principle after C5 that forbids cutting when the continuation resolves scope or polarity and also tells the model what a good cut looks like; addresses the primary finding about scope‑resolving continuations while avoiding a blanket verb–complement ban.

Insert a narrow, conditional verb–complement check after C5 to prevent cuts that split a verb/copula/auxiliary from an immediately required complement while avoiding a blanket ban that hurt very short fragments.

Insert a narrow, surface-level check after C5 forbidding cuts when the immediately following token is a scope-resolver, comparative, quantifier, percent/per, or begins with digits; keep that token attached to the left piece to avoid scope/polarity loss.

Insert a narrow surface-level rule after C5 that forbids cutting immediately before tokens that typically begin verb complements (determiners, demonstratives, possessives, object pronouns, quantifiers, or numerals), so a verb is not left separated from its immediately required object/measure.
Replace E1 with measured example en_us_738 to teach the model about negation + quantifier scope that resolves polarity and should not be cut.
Replace E2 with measured example en_us_936 to teach the model about conditional/subordinating scope ('Unless') that resolves truth conditions.
Replace E3 with measured example en_us_1116 to teach the model about exception clauses ('except') that reverse or limit prior claims.
Replace E4 with measured example en_us_103 to teach the model about numeral+unit and measurement phrases that determine scope and must stay attached.
Replace E1 with measured example en_us_30 to teach the model about cuts that separate auxiliaries/coping verbs from their complements (primary finding).
Replace E2 with measured example en_us_1543 to show cases where auxiliary + location/clause ('had been to X, where...') must not be split.
Replace E3 with measured example en_us_292 to illustrate verb+complement sequences ('resulting in', predicate completion) that should stay attached.
Replace E4 with measured example en_us_464 to demonstrate splits that break predicates and causative/contrast clauses harming cohesion.

Insert a narrow principle after C5: when the continuation will resolve scope or polarity, prefer cuts that include the scope-resolving token with the left piece; otherwise cut only at punctuation/clause boundaries that preserve a complete predicate — addresses the primary finding without a blanket ban.

Insert a narrow, surface-level check after C5 to prevent cutting a verb/auxiliary/copula away from an immediately following token that visibly begins a noun or measurement phrase (determiner, demonstrative, possessive, object pronoun, numeral/digit, or capitalized proper name); this targets the verb‑split primary finding without a blanket ban.
